title: Review of c01's Marangoni droplets finding: no self-propulsion on seed 7 in any arm (max 0.6-2.1 BL), as claimed; alpha=-20 lowers division, but alpha=+20 gives more bodies with fewer persistent splits
summary: Fresh labkit runs of the finding's world.py on seed 7 (128^2, T=20000) with ampf=0.05 (the force scale the summary names; world.py's default is 1.0 and the packs' commands do not record the override) at alpha = 0, +20, -20. No arm self-propels: max 1.4, 2.1 and 0.6 body lengths, max speeds 0.0035, 0.0074 and 0; every arm ends as a static droplet lattice (a20/sheet.png from t~10000). Division: alpha=0 14 splits, 14 persistent, generation 3, 16 bodies at the end; alpha=+20 28 splits, 10 persistent, generation 3, 22 bodies (the early flow fragments droplets, t=800-3500); alpha=-20 6 splits, 6 persistent, generation 2, 8 bodies. The negative result for M replicates; the division effect has the claimed sign for alpha=-20 and for final body count at +20, but not for persistent splits at +20 (10 vs 14 at alpha=0).

observations.I: a0/sheet.png: discrete round droplets, 16 at the end
observations.D: a0/lineage.png and FACTS: 14 persistent splits, generation 3, 0 merges (from 2 planted droplets); absence of M: max 1.4/2.1/0.6 BL across the three arms

controls_run.D: a0/ (alpha=0 passive Korteweg stress, same solver) against a20/ and a-20/

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. The persistent-split increase at alpha=+20 does not replicate (10 vs 14), though the final body count does (22 vs 16); the finding's main negative result (no swimming) does. Runs start from 2 planted droplets, not noise. world.py's default ampf=1.0 is the violent screen setting, so reproducing the packs needs WORLD_P ampf=0.05, which the pack commands omit.
